prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, budget, the type/size of system you need, and whether you value lowest price, long warranties, or faster scheduling. I can help you find the best option for your situation if you tell me your ZIP code and a few details (see questions below). Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical guide to pick the best contractor to replace your AC.

Quick checklist of what really matters
- Licensed and insured in Georgia. Ask for license number.  
- NATE-certified technicians (or equivalent) and manufacturer training for the brand they install.  
- Performs a Manual J load calculation and measures airflow — proper sizing/installation matters more than brand.  
- Offers clear written contract: scope, model numbers, SEER rating, start/end dates, permit responsibility, disposal of old unit.  
- Parts and labor warranty (get terms in writing). Compressor warranty length and whether they register it for you.  
- Good local reviews (Google, BBB, Angi). Ask for recent local references.  
- Permits and code compliance — contractor should handle permits.  
- Financing options and maintenance plans if you want them.

Well-known companies you’ll commonly find in Atlanta
- Coolray (large regional company, 24/7 service)  
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (national franchise network, punctuality guarantees)  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (national, full-service)  
- Local authorized dealers for Carrier, Lennox, Trane — these often provide factory-backed warranties and certified installers

(Those are common reputable options, but a smaller local company with excellent reviews and proven experience on installations in your neighborhood may be the best choice.)

Questions to ask any contractor before hiring
1. Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? What’s your license number?  
2. Do you perform Manual J load calculations and include that in the quote?  
3. What brand and model do you recommend and why? What SEER will it have?  
4. What is included in the price (equipment, labor, permits, disposal, startup and testing)?  
5. How long are parts and labor warranties? Are compressor and labor warranties transferable?  
6. Will you register the manufacturer warranty for me?  
7. Do you offer any maintenance plans?  
8. Can you provide references for installations in my neighborhood?  
9. What is the project timeline and payment schedule?  
10. Do you have emergency/after-hours service?

If you want, I can:
- Give a short list of top-rated contractors near you (tell me your ZIP or neighborhood), or  
- Draft an email/script you can use to request quotes from multiple companies.

Which would you prefer?
